origin: A real Codex CLI rollout reduced to the shapes a sequence reading turns on: the harness's own developer and user messages before any model output, a turn opened by a reasoning item and continued by an assistant message, two tool calls, and one patch applying to six files at once. Redacted by field allowlist: every token counter, every line count and every file count is verbatim; session and call ids are stand-ins, paths are stand-ins, and each prompt, completion, tool input and tool output became the same number of placeholder lines. session_meta.source is kept because the scope a sequence is read under depends on it; the whole event kinds the reading does not use are dropped rather than redacted.
method: Counted from the raw JSONL with jq, never calling internal/parser. Two token_count events carry the cumulative totals every per-turn figure is differenced from, and the 22 lines are few enough to check by reading them.

derivations.records: 2 token_count events, each advancing the cumulative counters. A turn is the delta between consecutive events, never the event's own numbers.
derivations.input_tokens: 16,180. Turn 1 advances input_tokens to 14,910 with 11,008 of it cached, leaving 3,902 uncached; turn 2 advances it by 26,358 with 14,080 cached, leaving 12,278. The two stored classes add back up to the input the counters gained: 16,180 + 25,088 = 41,268.
derivations.cache_read_tokens: 25,088 = 11,008 + 14,080, the cached share of each turn's input delta.
derivations.reasoning_tokens: 92 = 39 + 53. A part of output, never added to it.
derivations.cache_write_tokens: Codex publishes no cache-write counter; its depth row does not claim the signal.
derivations.cache_write_1h_tokens: no cache write, so no tier of one.
derivations.lines_added: 132 '+' body lines across the six file updates in the single patch_apply_end. Every change here is an 'update' carrying a unified diff; none is a creation, so none contributes a whole-file body.
derivations.lines_removed: 0. The six diffs are pure additions -- no '-' line inside any hunk.
derivations.rework_lines: 0. Nothing this window added is removed again by it.
derivations.edits: 1 applied patch. Codex counts a patch application, not a file, which is why this is 1 where the sequence below holds 6.
derivations.tool_calls: 3: two named calls (both 'exec') plus the patch application, which Codex records as an event rather than as a named write tool.
derivations.rejected: Codex does not record tool-use denials -- a documented gap, not a zero.
derivations.tool_errors: 0. Both calls carry status 'completed' and the patch succeeded.
derivations.compactions: no compaction boundary in this window.
derivations.steps: 10: one assistant step per turn (2), one per named tool call (2), and one per file the patch touched (6). The three developer messages and the two user messages open nothing -- they are the turn's input, not the model's output, and an assistant step placed on one of them would sit before the work it describes. The assistant message on line 13 opens no second step either: its turn was already opened by the reasoning item before it.
derivations.step_outcomes: 6 of the 10 state how they ended, and all six are the patched files: patch_apply_end says whether it applied. The two calls do not, and that is the point -- Codex marks a call 'completed' when it returns, which is not the same word as succeeded, so reading it as ok would publish a success the log never claimed. The two assistant steps carry no stop reason at all.
derivations.step_targets: 6: each file the patch named gets its own integer, assigned in first-seen order within this sequence. The two 'exec' calls name no file -- their input is a command, which is content this reading never opens.
derivations.skipped: every line is valid JSON and every payload is a shape the reader recognises -- including the session_meta whose 'source' is a bare string here, the form 2,500 of 2,507 rollouts on the audited corpus use.
